children.title: Causal-Guided Adaptive Editing for Foundational Assumptions

detail.title: Causal-Guided Adaptive Editing for Foundational Assumptions
detail.summary: Causal-guided adaptive knowledge editing (CAKE) provides a mechanism for localizing and adjusting foundational premises in LLMs. By mapping causal dependencies, agents can potentially prune or refine erroneous axioms that propagate through reasoning chains. This methodology is particularly relevant for addressing foundational assumptions that are not explicitly defined but implicitly govern agent behavior.
detail.reason: Expanding the synthesis of foundational premise correction using CAKE evidence.

children.title: Frameworks for Autonomous Reasoning Error Attribution

detail.title: Frameworks for Autonomous Reasoning Error Attribution
detail.summary: Reasoning blind spots often arise from implicit, unchecked assumptions embedded in model training. By leveraging causal editing, we can isolate the specific reasoning nodes that lead to circular or biased logic. This framework aids in attribution but does not automatically remediate all classes of meta-reasoning failure.
detail.reason: Applying CAKE to the problem of reasoning error attribution.
